newsitem.title: GERMANY: Competition hots up in German domestic air travel.
newsitem.headline: Competition hots up in German domestic air travel.

text.p: Competition hotted up in the German air travel market on Monday as Deutsche Lufthansa AG and Deutsche BA both announced cuts to fares on domestic routes.

Lufthansa said it was reducing its fares on the routes Munich-Hamburg, Munich-Cologne/Bonn, Munich-Duesseldorf, Munich-Berlin, Cologne/Bonn-Berlin, Stuttgart-Berlin and Duesseldorf-Berlin to as low as 222 marks.
The cuts amount to savings from 38 marks on the lowest fare to 120 marks on certain business class fares.

Deutsche BA, the airline 49 percent-owned by British Airways Plc and which only in January announced a new fare structure, immediately issued a statement saying it was shaving prices on its Munich-Hamburg route.

It said it was cutting 100 marks off its most flexible fare on that route, bringing it to 550 marks for a limited period, while the so-called "value-ticket", which has to be booked at least a week in advance, will fall 30 marks to 290.
Deutsche BA also has a 190 mark "super-value-ticket" bookable two weeks in advance.
A Lufthansa spokeswoman said the fare reductions were in response to competition on those routes, noting however that they were already loss-making for it at current prices.
The cuts do not apply to the Frankfurt-Berlin route, on which Deutsche BA does not compete, and on which Lufthansa was warned by German cartel authorities last month that it was charging too much.
